es: Adaptar un mensaje de viaje al lector británico o estadounidense y usar palabras neutras cuando no conoces su variedad.

teaching.en: For my British friend I write trainers, but for my American friend I write sneakers.
teaching.es: Para mi amigo británico escribo trainers, pero para mi amigo estadounidense escribo sneakers.
teaching.explanationEs: Adaptar el vocabulario al lector evita malentendidos.

prompt.es: Reescribe el mensaje de viaje para un lector británico y otro estadounidense.

answer.text: For a British reader: Hi! We are going on holiday next week. We will take the lift to the flat, wait in the queue and put our luggage in the boot. Please bring trainers and a jumper. For an American reader: Hi! We are going on vacation next week. We will take the elevator to the apartment, wait in line and put our luggage in the trunk. Please bring sneakers and a sweater.
accepted: For a British reader: Hi! We are going on holiday next week. We will take the lift to the flat, wait in the queue and put our luggage in the boot. Please bring trainers and a jumper. For an American reader: Hi! We are going on vacation next week. We will take the elevator to the apartment, wait in line and put our luggage in the trunk. Please bring sneakers and a sweater.

British reader: Hello! We go on holiday next week. We take the lift up to the flat, stand in the queue and leave our luggage in the boot. Bring trainers and a jumper, please. American reader: Hello! We go on vacation next week. We take the elevator up to the apartment, stand in line and leave our luggage in the trunk. Bring sneakers and a sweater, please.

feedback.es: Cada versión usa el vocabulario de su lector: holiday, lift, flat, queue, boot, trainers y jumper para el británico; vacation, elevator, apartment, line, trunk, sneakers y sweater para el estadounidense.

origin.text: Hi! We are going on holiday next week. We will take the lift to the flat, wait in the queue, and put our luggage in the boot. Please bring trainers and a jumper.
